name: Character Sheet · 角色设定
description: Build a consistent character reference sheet / 制作人物角色设定图
instructions:
## Purpose
Create an ordinary character reference sheet. Respond in the user's language. Default to natural standing poses, not A-pose or T-pose. This workflow produces reference artwork, not rigged models or animation-ready separated layers.

## Inputs
Use the character description, outfit, visual style and optional reference images. Inspect supplied references with view_image before making visual claims. Ask only about missing information that materially affects the result; state reasonable defaults briefly for other details. If sources conflict, clarify which design takes precedence. Do not mistake multiple characters for views of one character.

## Outputs
One consistent character reference sheet; default three views, no rigged or separated animation assets.

## Steps
Establish fixed traits
Briefly summarize the identity to preserve: face shape, silhouette, body proportions, hair shape and color, clothing structure, footwear, materials, palette, accessory count and placement. Record asymmetric features using the CHARACTER'S own left and right, not the viewer's. Hidden back or side details are design completions: keep them consistent with visible construction and disclose this inference rather than claiming they were observed.

Choose views and layout
Default deliverable: ONE sheet showing front, one true side profile, and back of the SAME character, in that order. Use the side that best reveals important features. For meaningful asymmetry, recommend adding the opposite side; retain the default unless the user accepts or has already requested both sides. For four views, explicitly describe front, character-left profile, back, character-right profile. Describe profile facing direction in the image prompt: a character-left profile exposes the character's left side and faces toward the viewer's left; character-right faces toward the viewer's right. A three-quarter view must not substitute for a side profile.
Use full-body natural upright standing, neutral expression, arms slightly separated from the torso, and enough separation between legs to read the silhouette. Keep pose, scale and proportions consistent. Align head tops, major body landmarks and foot baselines. Leave clear gaps between views; no overlap or cropping of hair, hands, feet or accessories. Prefer a simple neutral background and an uncluttered horizontal layout with enough room for each view. Do not claim an aspect ratio is enforced unless supported by the actual tool.

Generate
Briefly explain the fixed traits and planned views. If the user has already requested generation and inputs suffice, proceed without an extra confirmation round; obey any application-required approval. Use create_images with output_mode=compose, count=1 for a single multi-view sheet. Repeat the same identifying traits across all views in the image prompt. Keep rendering style, line weight, lighting and detail level consistent. Avoid dramatic perspective, action poses, scenery, strong cast shadows, new outfit variants or invented decorative accessories. Do not add labels, text, watermarks or annotations by default; preserve intentional markings already specified in the character design.
If separate files are requested, use separate count=1 tool calls with view-specific prompts and the appropriate references, never a prompt asking one image request for multiple files. Keep the total within the 3-image task budget. Four separate view files require another task; explain this before generating rather than silently omitting a view. Preserve originals.

## Acceptance
After generation, use view_image to inspect the actual result. Check the number and direction of views, missing or duplicate angles, face and body proportions, hair and clothing consistency, accessory count and left/right placement, limb anatomy, framing, overlap, alignment, and whether side/back construction matches the front. Report concrete issues and uncertainty; successful tool execution is not proof of visual correctness. If inspection is unavailable or the task budget is exhausted, say the result is unverified. Ask before additional paid revisions and do not regenerate automatically. Do not promise exact lettering, pixel-perfect consistency, transparency or exact dimensions without verification. The user makes the final visual judgment.

## Limits
Optional extensions
Expression sheets, alternate outfits, palette cards, prop details and close-ups are separate follow-up deliverables only when requested. Do not pack them into the default sheet.
